title: Independent ARC testing shows Astra's result depends heavily on its harness
friendlyTitle: Astra's test score changed a lot with different supporting software
summary: ARC Prize measured GPT-6 Astra at 62.7% on its semi-private ARC-AGI-3 tasks with the standard harness and 99.9% with an OpenAI provider adapter that preserves hidden reasoning state and compacts long sessions. The model used fewer actions than the median tested human on 96% of levels, but ARC Prize says this bounded benchmark is not proof of AGI.
friendlySummary: Astra scored 62.7% with a standard setup and 99.9% with OpenAI's special setup on the same AI reasoning test. The researchers say the result does not prove that the model is AGI.
whyItMatters: The large gap between harnesses is a reminder that memory, compaction and tool design can change agent performance as much as model choice. Buyers should ask how benchmark runs were configured and evaluate the full deployed system, not treat one headline score as a portable property of the model.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The software around an AI model can greatly change its results. Compare complete working systems, not only one impressive score.
